what_it_does: Server software has enormous instruction working sets (the code is huge), causing the processor to frequently stall waiting for instructions to arrive from memory—a bottleneck even modern prefetching doesn't fully solve. Current prefetchers record the exact sequence of instructions executed and replay that pattern, but this fails when the code takes a different path than predicted. This paper proposes Hierarchical Prefetching, which groups related code regions into larger functional blocks called Bundles (tens to hundreds of kilobytes of code). When the processor detects entry into a Bundle, the hardware prefetches the entire Bundle rather than individual instructions. The Bundle groupings are computed once during offline analysis of the server binary, and most Bundle metadata lives in main memory, so only a tiny 2KB of on-chip cache is needed to track which Bundles are active.
